newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Market sees some demand for jet.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Market sees some demand for jet.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel was traded on Tuesday as the market expected some demand emerging from China and Indonesia, which might limit the recent free-fall at least for the moment, traders said.
China was said to be negotiating for at least two jet fuel cargoes for March delivery, which traders said could absorb any surplus cargoes resulting from the recent slow demand.
Traders said a Singapore trader who bought 100,000 barrels of jet fuel at $26.80 for second-half March lifting fob from a German trader, might be positioning itself for sales to Indonesia.
Traders said this was a good price as it indicated a 10-cent rise over the previous deal last week.
The trader was also negotiating to buy from a Mediterranean trader at $26.60 per barrel but the deal fell through due to disagreements over color specifications.
The swaps jet-gas oil regrade has narrowed to $1.30/$1.50 a barrel, down from Monday's $1.50/$1.80.

Gas oil swaps fell 30 cents on overnight crude weakness, but physical values held steady with an offer seen at $25.15 with a bid at $25.45. A 220,000-barrel cargo was traded between two European majors at a 20-cent-per-barrel premium to Singapore quotes for March 23-27 lifting fob.
Traders said sales into China have been sporadic while some activity has been seen in Hong Kong after a recent lull.
